# PMI-scope claim definition: evidence and proposal

Decision gate 2 (`AGENTS.md`), issue #8. This is evidence and a recommendation, not a decision. The
starting position is `_docs/plan.md` section 2.4.1. No claim counts are built until the user signs
off (issue #15).

All figures are unweighted event-file totals in US dollars (nominal, not on-levelled), except the
"Weighted share" column in the first tables. Every table is generated by
`uv run python -m health_pricing.evidence.pmi_scope` from the DuckDB raw tables, so the numbers below
can be reproduced. Source: AHRQ MEPS HC-243 and HC-251 (full-year files) and HC-239D/F/G and
HC-248D/F/G (event files).

A data fix was needed first. The M1 loader divided event costs and weights by 10^decimals even though
AHRQ stores them with literal decimal points, so event costs were 100 times too small and weights 10^6
times too small. This is fixed (commit `9e2bf6c`). Event-file totals now agree with the FYC category
totals to within 0.01% for inpatient, outpatient and office-based, and the weights sum to 333.1 million
(2022) and 334.5 million (2023).

## Summary

- The proposal confirms six of the seven rows in the section 2.4.1 table (inpatient with one change)
  and argues against one (hospital outpatient as a blanket "in"). It adds a birth exclusion for
  inpatient stays and a laser eye surgery exclusion.
- It captures 36.4% (2022) and 39.3% (2023) of total spending, and 65.1% and 68.3% of the cost of the
  three event files. This passes the "clear minority to moderate share" sense check.
- 41.5% (2022) and 43.0% (2023) of persons have at least one in-scope claim. This is a US utilisation
  level and is probably higher than a UK PMI book. The models use relativities, so it matters for the
  claim count but not for the factor shapes. State it in the README.
- Two judgement calls are left for the user. They are the technician and physiotherapy visits, and
  stays that began in the emergency room.

## Verdict on each row of the section 2.4.1 table

| Row | Starting position | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inpatient stays (incl. day-case) | In | **Confirm, with one change.** Exclude birth and pregnancy stays | Stays with `RSNINHOS` 4, 5 or 6 are 7.3% (2022) and 6.4% (2023) of inpatient cost. UK PMI usually excludes maternity. |
| Hospital outpatient department | In | **Argue against a blanket "in".** Apply the same specialty and visit rules as office-based | 28.5% (2022) and 29.3% (2023) of outpatient cost fails the rules. General checkups are 9.5% of 2023 cost (`VSTCTGRY` 1), and general practice, family practice, internal medicine and paediatrics are 4.6%. Hospital clinics also record nurses and technicians who are not specialists. |
| Office-based, specialist physician | In | **Confirm** | Specialist `DRSPLTY_M18` levels hold the diagnosis and treatment visits that map to a private consultant appointment. |
| Office-based, GP or primary care | Out | **Confirm** | Family practice, general practice, internal medicine and paediatrics are 13.4% (2022) and 14.8% (2023) of office-based cost. |
| ER visit | Out | **Confirm** | ER is 3.1% (2022) and 3.3% (2023) of total spending. See the caveat on stays that began in the ER below. |
| Prescribed medicines | Out | **Confirm** | 25.0% (2022) and 24.1% (2023) of total spending. Whether drugs given during a stay sit inside inpatient cost has not been tested here. |
| Dental, optical, home health | Out | **Confirm** | Dental is 5.3% and 5.5%. Home health, glasses and other medical are 10.7% and 9.6% (the "Other" row). |

## Verdict on each guidance bullet

- **Provider specialty (`DRSPLTY_M18`). Confirm.** Family practice (6), general practice (8), internal
  medicine (14) and paediatrician (24) are out. All other specialties are in, including geriatrics (10),
  which is immaterial at under 0.1% of cost. "Other specialty" (91) is in, because it is not primary
  care and holds 4.1% to 5.8% of office-based cost. Unknown specialty (-8, -7) is out, because a
  specialist visit cannot be shown. Level -1 means the visit was to a non-doctor, so the type seen decides.
- **Visit category (`VSTCTGRY`). Confirm.** General checkup (1), immunisations (6), vision exam (7),
  pregnancy-related (8), well-child exam (9) and laser eye surgery (10) are out. These are 26.3% (2022)
  and 26.8% (2023) of office-based cost. Laser eye surgery is added to the starting list because UK PMI
  treats it as elective. Emergency (3), diagnosis or treatment (2), follow-up (5), other (91) and unknown
  codes stay in when the specialty qualifies.
- **Grey areas, decided explicitly.** Non-physician providers and psychiatric care are decided below.
- **Sense check. Pass.** 36.4% and 39.3% of total spending is a moderate share.

## Grey area 1: non-physician providers

Visits to non-doctors (level -1 of `DRSPLTY_M18`) are 48.9% (2022) and 47.3% (2023) of office-based
cost, so this choice matters.

| Type seen (`MEDPTYPE_M18`) | Recommendation | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Physical or occupational therapist (10) | In | UK PMI covers physiotherapy, usually with a session limit. 19.9% of 2023 non-doctor cost. |
| Psychologist (13) | In | UK PMI covers psychological therapy on referral, usually with a limit. 3.4% of 2023 non-doctor cost. |
| Technician (15) | In, flagged | The best fit is diagnostics, which section 2.4.1 puts in. 19.1% of 2023 non-doctor cost. |
| Nurse or nurse practitioner (8), physician's assistant (11) | Out | These act as US primary care and are the equivalent of a GP practice. |
| Mental health counsellor or family therapist (6), social worker (14) | Out | Counselling without a clinician referral is rarely a PMI claim. |
| Chiropractor (2), acupuncturist (1), massage (5), alternative (4) | Out | Complementary cover is a limited add-on in UK PMI. |
| Optometrist (9), dentist (3), podiatrist (12), midwife (7) | Out | Eye care, dental and maternity are separate or excluded. |
| Other (91), unknown (-8, -7, -15) | Out | A specialist visit cannot be shown. |

Sensitivity. If every non-doctor type is out, the captured share of total spending falls from 36.4% to
30.1% (2022) and from 39.3% to 33.2% (2023). If only psychologist visits stay in, it falls to 30.6% and
33.6%. The share stays a moderate minority either way.

## Grey area 2: psychiatric care

Recommendation. Include psychiatry (specialty 28) and psychologist visits, and keep visit category 4
(psychotherapy and mental health counselling) in when the specialty or type seen qualifies. UK PMI
usually covers mental health, with limits that are product features, not part of the claim definition.
Visit category 4 is 8.9% (2022) and 8.3% (2023) of office-based cost. Excluding it altogether would
lower the captured share of total spending by under one point (35.5% and 38.4%).

## Caveat: stays that began in the emergency room

Stays with `EMERROOM` = 1 are 51.0% (2022) and 45.4% (2023) of inpatient cost. The plan counts them as
inpatient, because the admission follows the ER visit, and the proposal keeps them in. A UK reviewer
could argue that an emergency admission through NHS A&E would not reach a private insurer. Removing these
stays would lower the captured share of total spending by up to 9.1 points (2022) and 9.9 points (2023).
This is the second judgement call for the user.

## Proposed definition

An event is a PMI-scope claim when it meets the rule for its file. The full level by level list is in
the last four tables. The rules are implemented once, in `src/health_pricing/evidence/pmi_scope.py`.

1. **Inpatient.** Every stay, except `RSNINHOS` 4 (birth, mother), 5 (to be born, baby) and 6
   (pregnancy complications). Stays that began in the ER stay in.
2. **Hospital outpatient and office-based.** An event counts when both parts hold.
   - The provider qualifies. This means a doctor whose `DRSPLTY_M18` is a specialty other than 6, 8, 14
     and 24 and is not unknown, or a non-doctor (`DRSPLTY_M18` = -1) whose `MEDPTYPE_M18` is 10, 13 or 15.
   - The visit category (`VSTCTGRY`) is not 1, 6, 7, 8, 9 or 10.
3. **Everything else is out.** This covers ER events not followed by admission, prescribed medicines,
   dental, vision, home health and other medical spending.
4. **Cost.** The event expenditure variable (`IPXP`, `OPXP`, `OBXP`) is the claim cost. It is the sum of
   facility and physician payments from all sources.

## What the proposal captures

| Year | Share of total spending (`TOTEXP`) | Share of the three event files | Persons with an in-scope claim |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 36.4% | 65.1% | 9,302 of 22,431 (41.5%) |
| 2023 | 39.3% | 68.3% | 8,127 of 18,919 (43.0%) |

Event-file totals reconcile to the FYC category totals (`IPTEXP`, `OPTEXP`, `OBVEXP`) to within 0.01%.

## Limitations to state in the README

- Claim frequency is a US level. The claimant share is 41% to 43% of persons.
- The definition uses event type, provider and visit category. It cannot model UK exclusions by
  condition, such as chronic or pre-existing conditions.
- Whether an event is a specialist referral or a self-booked visit is not recorded.

## Decisions needed from the user

1. Approve the definition above, or change it.
2. Technician and physiotherapy visits: in (recommended) or out.
3. Stays that began in the ER: in (recommended, as the plan says) or out.

Psychiatric care, the change to hospital outpatient and the exclusion of birth-related stays follow the
recommendations above unless the user says otherwise.
